chunks: O you who believe, remember the favours of God to you when an army came against you and We sent a wind against them and forces that you did not see. But God sees all that you do.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the unseen forces sent during the Battle of the Confederates in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the Battle of the Confederates (Ghazwah al-Ahzab), where God’s unseen forces (junud) and the biting wind served as divine intervention to preserve the community. It highlights the concept of 'unseen victory' (nasr ghayr mar'wi), reinforcing the belief that God’s help is not limited to visible military might but includes spiritual and natural signs, a theme frequently cited in discussions of Imam Ali’s leadership during this period.
